references.text: The background to Abraham's distress: Sarah sees Ishmael laughing and demands that Abraham send away Hagar and her son.
God's direct response to Abraham's distress: God reassures him and says he should listen to Sarah, but that Ishmael will also become a nation.
Abraham's prayer that Ishmael might live before God's face, showing his deep love for Ishmael and explaining his pain in 21:11.
Ishmael's birth and Abraham's role as father – Abraham was 86 years old when Ishmael was born, and had a close relationship with him for many years.

Paul explains that not all of Abraham's descendants are his children in the sense of the promise – 'through Isaac your offspring shall be named' – which sheds light on God's plan behind Sarah's demand.
The Epistle to the Hebrews highlights the theological significance of Abraham's pain and trial mentioned in Genesis.
